key_insight: The paper shows that large language models contain functionally specialized subnetworks with very low overlap, and that isolating updates to these regions can improve continual learning while reducing catastrophic forgetting.
engineering_relevance: For AI systems that must adapt over time, localized parameter updates offer a more efficient and stable alternative to full-model retraining, preserving prior capabilities under sequential learning.
method: Use gradient-attribution profiling to identify cognition-associated functional subnetworks.
Route each training example to its corresponding subnetwork for targeted adaptation.
Restrict parameter updates and optimizer states to the selected regions in CiMEO.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on 1.4 million sequential instructions and achieved the best average performance across five generative benchmarks covering programming, exam-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning.
watch_item: Subnetwork localization and routing add implementation complexity, and the approach depends on accurately identifying task-relevant regions without missing shared representations.
paper_title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
